prev_row.boundary_rationale: A single verse announces a cosmic judgment with its own ba-yom-hahu formula, “In that day, Yahweh… will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan, the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea” (web:Isa.27.1), matching בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) for the onset and עַ֤ל לִוְיָתָן֙ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier), ‘upon Leviathan.’ A setumah (single-witness) follows this verse in the parashah layer, and the vineyard-song frame of Isa.27.2 opens a distinct, separately quoted unit. The onset formula itself, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier), recurs at exactly 3 verses book-wide at this same accented form (sweep: 3 verses); it does not by itself distinguish this verse from Isa.27.2, which opens the identical formula at accent_stripped tier (בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא, oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier in its own verse). What separates them is what follows the formula: here a complete verbal clause with its own divine subject, יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier), while at Isa.27.2 the formula is followed first by a noun phrase, כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), opening a vineyard-summons that only completes across the following verses; the parashah layer marks the difference too, bracketing this verse alone with a setumah on both edges (after Isa.26.21 and after Isa.27.1), where the next closing mark after Isa.27.2 falls at Isa.27.6.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A restoration promise opens on a bare participial onset, not a dated formula in the bytes themselves — “In days to come, Jacob will take root. The argument continues through Isa.27.7's third-masculine-singular suffixes and Isa.27.8's third-feminine-singular suffixes, both read as referring back to Jacob and Israel of Isa.27.6 though carried by two different suffix classes rather than one repeated pronoun, through the atonement clause “the iniquity of Jacob will be forgiven” (web:Isa.27.9), matching יְכֻפַּ֣ר עֲוֺֽן יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.9, byte tier), and on to a contrastive judgment on an unnamed fortified city (web:Isa.27.10, web:Isa.27.11) offered as a foil to Jacob's own measured discipline. Isa.27.12 opens its own ba-yom-hahu formula, a fresh frame this row does not share.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A single verse carries its own ba-yom-hahu onset, “It will happen in that day that Yahweh will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt” (web:Isa.27.12), matching וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier). Isa.27.13 opens a second, independent instance of the same formula with a different image (trumpet rather than threshing), so the repeated onset is read as two proclamations rather than one unit spanning both verses; a setumah (single-witness) separates the two in the parashah layer.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Isa.27.12 and Isa.27.13 into one ingathering row was considered, since both share the same destination image, but rejected: the two onsets agree only at accent_stripped tier — וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier) differ from each other in their accents — and each introduces a distinct image, threshing against the trumpet, with a single-witness setumah recorded after oshb:Isa.27.12 (tier-3, non-driving) standing between the two. The waw prefixed on both onsets is a sequencing form and could as readily support reading the pair as one continuing announcement; that rival is weighed and set aside because both halves are complete on their own terms and the mark, however weak, falls exactly at the image change.

A scroll-noun catchword crosses this row's front seam: הַסֵּ֣פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) and סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Isa.29.12, byte tier) recur at consonantal-skeleton tier in דִּבְרֵי סֵ֑פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.18, byte tier), the noun's skeleton standing at exactly 4 verses in Isa.28-31 (oshb:Isa.29.11, oshb:Isa.29.12, oshb:Isa.29.18, oshb:Isa.30.8) and 20 book-wide. prev_row.boundary_rationale: A doubled imperative opens this row, הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ (oshb:Isa.29.9, byte tier), “Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind!” (web:Isa.29.9), a fresh imperative onset (four forms) after the deliverance unit closing at web:Isa.29.8. The blindness announced there is illustrated by the sealed-book simile “All vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed” (web:Isa.29.11, a ketiv/qere-bearing verse at Isa.29.11, quoted here up to the point before its varying token). The speech-frame וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י (oshb:Isa.29.13, byte tier), a divine frame, continues the same indictment of lip-service worship rather than opening a fresh unit: the indictment's object continues from the blinded people of Isa.29.9-Isa.29.12 even as the person-marking turns from second-person plural to third-person report, and no fresh frame opens between them. The row closes on “the understanding of their prudent men will be hidden.” (web:Isa.29.14), the verse just before the next hoy onset at web:Isa.29.15.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would open a fresh unit at the divine speech-frame וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י (oshb:Isa.29.13, byte tier) rather than holding it with the blindness oracle that precedes it; it is rejected because the indictment's object continues from Isa.29.9-Isa.29.12 and no fresh frame separates the two.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: oracle of spiritual blindness built around the sealed-book simile and an indictment of hollow worship
